claims.claim_en: Adjective from the root علم, meaning 'Knowing' / 'All‑knowing' (attribute of God).
Proper name 'Allah' (conventional derivation associated with the notion of deity; often discussed as related to اله).
claims.needs_review_reason: Etymology of 'Allah' is debated; classical derivation from the root اله is conventional but contested among scholars — flagged for review.

claims.claim_en: Imperative/command form (root قول/قَالَ) used to introduce an address: 'Say!'
An imperative/jussive plural sense from the semantic field of موت/مات meaning 'die!' — here rhetorical/strong exhortation.
claims.needs_review_reason: The specific Qur'anic form 'مُوتُوا' is rhetorically forceful and its precise morphological classification (imperative vs. jussive exhortation) may require review by a classical sarf/i'rab source.

claims.claim_en: From the root أمن (لأَمِنَ/ءَامَنَ) meaning 'to believe' / 'have faith'; here present indicative/imperfect plural 'you believe'.
Perfect (past) first‑person plural of root أمن meaning 'we believed'.
